reasoning: The attempts are nearly identical in design: server-side ownership tables, a rate and reach helper shared by placing and removing, the occupied cell cleared on removal, a right-click drag threshold, and a single-finger long press on Begin. A adds a small IsA check and a right-click duration limit, but it fails stylua --check on its own code. B passes every check, so B wins.

criteria.note: Changes stay in BlockPlacement.server.luau and BlockPlacer.luau, with the existing style and helper extraction (checkRateAndReach, raycastFromScreen).
The server-side `blocks[part]` record stores ownerUserId, and onRemoveBlock refuses when `record.ownerUserId ~= player.UserId`; the attribute is only a client hint.
Checks typeof Instance and IsA BasePart, requires a server record (only blocks the server placed), runs checkRateAndReach on record.cell, and clears occupied[record.cell].
MouseButton2 down/up with summed drag deltas plus a 0.4 s duration limit, TouchLongPress on Begin with one finger, and gameProcessedEvent skipped; placing still works.
Logic is correct and luau-lsp and selene pass, but stylua --check fails on its own long `if` line in removeAt.
Edits only the two placement files in their existing style, extracting canEditCell and raycastFromScreen.
`placedBlocks[block].OwnerUserId` is compared to player.UserId on the server; the attribute is commented as client-only.
typeof Instance check, then a placedBlocks lookup that proves the part is a block the server placed, canEditCell for rate and reach, and occupied[placed.Cell] cleared.
Right-click with a drag threshold through InputChanged/InputEnded, TouchLongPress on Begin with one finger, and gameProcessed input ignored; tap and click still place.
All checks pass (luau-lsp, selene, StyLua) and changes stay in scope.

strengths: Ownership check uses only the server-side table
Shared rate limit across placing and removing
Right-click separated from camera drag by distance and duration
Blocks folder found once in start()
weaknesses: StyLua formatting fails on its own code in removeAt

strengths: Server table lookup validates both block identity and ownership
weaknesses: No explicit IsA check on the server (the table lookup covers it)
Looks up the Blocks folder on every removal
